Non-limit exit → retry once then park (attempt-driven), no bundle transitions. Model-unavailable at spawn → dead {platform, model} added to avoidEntries, re-resolve to the SAME platform's next entry, relaunch, no seal/receive. Usage-limit → the ordered transaction on the REAL command machinery: loop position checkpointed into the bundle under the supervisor session BEFORE the seal; finalize with reasonClass usage-limit (degraded-open path also pinned); receive prepare+commit back-to-back with identical flags/session; zero .handoff/loop writes across the transaction (fs spy); injected window drift → one automatic re-prepare retry; second consecutive stale → park; relaunch assignment avoids the dead origin platform; total exhaustion → park with the classifier's resumeAt hint; deterministic from injected io. The test-author flags one design seam for your judgment: `hooks.beforeCommit()` — a test-only injection point used to mutate git state inside the prepare→commit window; production passes nothing.

    93	/**
    94	 * Scripted fake child runner honoring the injection seam. Each call shifts the
    95	 * next result off the queue, writes its logContent to opts.logPath (so the
    96	 * command reads the transcript from the child's LOG file), and records the
    97	 * spawn spec.
    98	 */
    99	function fakeRunner(io, script) {
   100	  const queue = [...script];
   101	  const calls = /** @type {any[]} */ ([]);
   102	  const fn = (/** @type {any} */ spec, /** @type {any} */ opts = {}) => {
   103	    calls.push({ spec, opts, args: spec?.args ?? [], command: spec?.command, env: spec?.env });
   104	    const r = queue.shift() ?? { timedOut: false, exitCode: 0, verdict: 'APPROVED', findings: '' };
   105	    const logPath = opts.logPath ?? `${loopPaths('/repo').dir}/children/fallback.log`;
   106	    if (typeof r.logContent === 'string') {
   107	      const dir = logPath.slice(0, logPath.lastIndexOf('/'));
   108	      io.fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
   109	      io.fs.writeFileSync(logPath, r.logContent);
   110	    }
   111	    return Promise.resolve({ timedOut: r.timedOut ?? false, exitCode: r.exitCode ?? 0, verdict: r.verdict ?? 'APPROVED', findings: r.findings ?? '', logPath });
   112	  };
   113	  fn.calls = calls;
   114	  return fn;
   115	}

    26	/**
    27	 * Assemble the spawn contract for a role child. Reviewers are read-only on
    28	 * every platform; every child is marked supervised (its own baton hooks
    29	 * no-op), carries the sole-author git identity, and has stdin CLOSED at
    30	 * spawn (the codex-exec stdin-hang field failure).
    31	 * @param {{platform: string, role: string, model: string, effort?: string | null, mode?: string}} assignment
    32	 * @param {string} prompt

    34	 * @returns {{command: string, args: string[], env: Record<string, string>, stdio: any[]}}
    35	 */
    36	export function buildChildArgv(assignment, prompt, opts) {
    37	  const readOnly = REVIEWER_ROLES.has(assignment.role);
    38	  const env = { BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD: '1', ...GIT_IDENTITY };

    58	const VERDICT_RE = /VERDICT:\s*(APPROVED_WITH_NOTES|APPROVED|BLOCKED)\b/g;
    59	
    60	/** @param {string} region @returns {{verdict: string, findings: string} | null} */
    61	function lastVerdictIn(region) {
    62	  let last = null;
    63	  for (const m of region.matchAll(VERDICT_RE)) last = m;
    64	  if (!last) return null;
    65	  const after = region.slice((last.index ?? 0) + last[0].length);
    66	  return { verdict: last[1], findings: after.trim() };
    67	}
    68	
    69	/**
    70	 * Region-bounded verdict parsing — the prompt region (which quotes the
    71	 * verdict format in its instructions) is NEVER scanned, and there is no
    72	 * whole-transcript fallback. Unparseable is BLOCKED, never APPROVED.
    73	 * - codex: only the text after the LAST line starting with 'tokens used'.
    74	 * - claude-code: only the `result` field of the structured JSON output.
    75	 * Multiple tails inside the trusted region → the LAST one wins.
    76	 * @param {string} transcript @param {{platform: string}} opts
    77	 * @returns {{verdict: string, findings: string, reason?: string}}
    78	 */
    79	export function parseVerdict(transcript, { platform }) {
    80	  const unparseable = { verdict: 'BLOCKED', findings: '', reason: 'unparseable' };
    81	  const text = String(transcript ?? '');
    82	
    83	  if (platform === 'claude-code') {
    84	    let obj = null;
    85	    try {
    86	      obj = JSON.parse(text.trim());
    87	    } catch {
    88	      return unparseable;
    89	    }
    90	    if (typeof obj?.result !== 'string') return unparseable;
    91	    const hit = lastVerdictIn(obj.result);
    92	    return hit ?? unparseable;
    93	  }
    94	
    95	  // codex: locate the LAST 'tokens used' marker line; the trusted region is
    96	  // strictly after it.
    97	  const lines = text.split('\n');
    98	  let markerLine = -1;
    99	  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i += 1) {
   100	    if (/^tokens used\b/i.test(lines[i])) markerLine = i;
   101	  }
   102	  if (markerLine === -1) return unparseable;
   103	  const region = lines.slice(markerLine + 1).join('\n');
   104	  const hit = lastVerdictIn(region);
   105	  return hit ?? unparseable;
   106	}
   107	
   108	const TRUNCATION_MARKER = '\n[... truncated by baton log cap ...]\n';
   109	
   110	/**
   111	 * Cap a transcript: head preserved, middle replaced with a marker, TAIL
   112	 * preserved verbatim (the verdict lives at the end and must never be cut).
   113	 * @param {string} text @param {number} maxBytes
   114	 * @returns {string}
   115	 */
   116	export function capLog(text, maxBytes) {
   117	  const s = String(text ?? '');
   118	  if (Buffer.byteLength(s) <= maxBytes) return s;
   119	  const headBytes = Math.max(1, Math.floor(maxBytes * 0.4));
   120	  const tailBytes = Math.max(1, maxBytes - headBytes);
   121	  const buf = Buffer.from(s);
   122	  const head = buf.subarray(0, headBytes).toString();
   123	  const tail = buf.subarray(buf.length - tailBytes).toString();
   124	  return head + TRUNCATION_MARKER + tail;
   125	}

   127	/**
   128	 * Exit classification delegates to core detect — one classifier, one
   129	 * signature table, no drift. Returns exactly classify(...).class.
   130	 * @param {string} transcript @param {number} exitCode @param {string} platform @param {any} table
   131	 * @returns {string}
   132	 */
   133	export function classifyChildExit(transcript, exitCode, platform, table) {
   134	  return classify({ text: transcript, exitCode, platform, table }).class;
   135	}

   137	/** @param {number} pid @param {NodeJS.Signals} sig */
   138	function killGroup(pid, sig) {
   139	  try {
   140	    process.kill(-pid, sig);
   141	  } catch {
   142	    // ESRCH — already gone.
   143	  }
   144	}
   145	
   146	/**
   147	 * Spawn and supervise one child: detached in its OWN process group, stdin
   148	 * closed; on timeout SIGTERM the group, wait graceMs, SIGKILL the group (no
   149	 * zombie grandchildren). Output streams to a capped log at opts.logPath; the
   150	 * verdict is parsed from the full transcript, region-bounded.
   151	 * @param {{command: string, args: string[], env?: Record<string, string>, cwd?: string}} spec
   152	 * @param {{timeoutMs: number, graceMs: number, logPath: string, maxLogBytes?: number, platform?: string}} opts
   153	 * @returns {Promise<{timedOut: boolean, exitCode: number | null, verdict?: string, findings?: string, reason?: string, logPath: string}>}
   154	 */
   155	export function superviseChild(spec, opts) {
   156	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
   157	    const maxLogBytes = opts.maxLogBytes ?? 1_000_000;
   158	    const child = spawn(spec.command, spec.args, {
   159	      cwd: spec.cwd,
   160	      env: { ...process.env, ...(spec.env ?? {}) },
   161	      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
   162	      detached: true, // its own process group — the kill unit
   163	    });
   164	
   165	    let out = '';
   166	    let timedOut = false;
   167	    /** @type {NodeJS.Timeout | null} */
   168	    let killTimer = null;
   169	
   170	    const onChunk = (/** @type {Buffer} */ c) => {
   171	      out += c.toString();
   172	    };
   173	    child.stdout?.on('data', onChunk);
   174	    child.stderr?.on('data', onChunk);
   175	
   176	    const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
   177	      timedOut = true;
   178	      if (typeof child.pid === 'number') {
   179	        killGroup(child.pid, 'SIGTERM');
   180	        killTimer = setTimeout(() => {
   181	          if (typeof child.pid === 'number') killGroup(child.pid, 'SIGKILL');
   182	        }, opts.graceMs);
   183	      }
   184	    }, opts.timeoutMs);
   185	
   186	    const finish = (/** @type {number | null} */ exitCode) => {
   187	      clearTimeout(timeout);
   188	      if (killTimer) clearTimeout(killTimer);
   189	      // Belt-and-braces: reap any group survivors even on a clean exit path.
   190	      if (timedOut && typeof child.pid === 'number') killGroup(child.pid, 'SIGKILL');
   191	      try {
   192	        mkdirSync(dirname(opts.logPath), { recursive: true });
   193	        writeFileSync(opts.logPath, capLog(out, maxLogBytes));
   194	      } catch {
   195	        // The log must never mask the result.
   196	      }
   197	      const parsed = parseVerdict(out, { platform: opts.platform ?? 'codex' });
   198	      resolve({
   199	        timedOut,
   200	        exitCode: timedOut ? null : exitCode,
   201	        verdict: parsed.verdict,
   202	        findings: parsed.findings,
   203	        ...(parsed.reason ? { reason: parsed.reason } : {}),
   204	        logPath: opts.logPath,
   205	      });
   206	    };
   207	
   208	    child.on('error', () => finish(null));
   209	    child.on('close', (code) => finish(code));
   210	  });
   211	}

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	/**
     2	 * Loop run state — snapshot + journal + replay for the Layer-2 supervisor,
     3	 * mirroring the bundle store's crash-tolerance idioms (atomic tmp+rename
     4	 * snapshots, torn-tail-tolerant NDJSON, seq-dedup replay). Everything lives
     5	 * under <root>/.handoff/loop/; the supervisor is the sole writer. Plan:
     6	 * docs/plans/2026-07-18-goal-loop-worktree-pipeline.md §"baton loop",
     7	 * §"Smoke gate", §"Supervisor lifetime and recovery", §"Caps".
     8	 */
     9	import { appendEntry, readAllTolerant } from '../util/jsonl.mjs';
    10	import { atomicWriteJson, safeReadJson, ensureDir } from '../util/fsx.mjs';
    11	import { dedupeKey } from '../util/ids.mjs';
    12	
    13	export const LOOP_STATE_SCHEMA = 'baton/loop-state@1';
    14	
    15	/** The frozen status vocabulary. */
    16	export const LOOP_STATUS = Object.freeze({
    17	  RUNNING: 'running',
    18	  AWAITING_SMOKE_APPROVAL: 'awaiting-smoke-approval',
    19	  PARKED: 'parked',
    20	  ESCALATED: 'escalated',
    21	  DONE: 'done',
    22	});
    23	
    24	/** The frozen journal event vocabulary. */
    25	export const LOOP_EVENT = Object.freeze({
    26	  PHASE_ADVANCE: 'phase-advance',
    27	  GATE_ITERATION: 'gate-iteration',
    28	  PARK: 'park',
    29	  RESUME: 'resume',
    30	  SMOKE_AWAIT: 'smoke-await',
    31	  SMOKE_APPROVE: 'smoke-approve',
    32	});
    33	
    34	// Every gate loops at most 5 times — a repo-wide hard invariant (AGENTS.md
    35	// §Review gates); the reducer refuses a 6th and escalates instead.
    36	const GATE_ITERATION_CAP = 5;
    37	
    38	/** @param {string} root */
    39	export function loopPaths(root) {
    40	  const dir = `${root}/.handoff/loop`;
    41	  return { dir, state: `${dir}/state.json`, journal: `${dir}/journal.ndjson` };
    42	}
    43	
    44	/**
    45	 * Fresh run state — pure and deterministic from the injected io (identity
    46	 * facts + clock only; no Date.now/Math.random, which would break replay).
    47	 * @param {any} spec a VALIDATED loop spec @param {any} io
    48	 */
    49	export function initLoopState(spec, io) {
    50	  const runId = `loop-${dedupeKey({ host: io.host, pid: io.pid, startTime: io.startTime, at: io.now() }).slice(0, 12)}`;
    51	  /** @type {Record<string, number>} */
    52	  const iterations = {};
    53	  for (const p of spec.phases ?? []) {
    54	    if (/gate/.test(String(p.id))) iterations[p.id] = 0;
    55	  }
    56	  return {
    57	    schema: LOOP_STATE_SCHEMA,
    58	    runId,
    59	    goal: spec.goal,
    60	    phaseCount: Array.isArray(spec.phases) ? spec.phases.length : 0,
    61	    phaseIndex: 0,
    62	    iterations,
    63	    status: LOOP_STATUS.RUNNING,
    64	    parkReason: null,
    65	    escalation: null,
    66	    smokeApproval: null,
    67	    createdAt: io.now(),
    68	    journalSeq: 0,
    69	  };
    70	}
    71	
    72	/**
    73	 * The pure transition reducer. Never mutates its input; unknown events and
    74	 * refused transitions return the input state unchanged (a new reference is
    75	 * only produced for a real transition).
    76	 * @param {any} state @param {any} ev
    77	 */
    78	export function applyLoopEvent(state, ev) {
    79	  switch (ev?.type) {
    80	    case LOOP_EVENT.PHASE_ADVANCE: {
    81	      const next = state.phaseIndex + 1;
    82	      if (next >= state.phaseCount) return { ...state, phaseIndex: state.phaseCount, status: LOOP_STATUS.DONE };
    83	      return { ...state, phaseIndex: next };
    84	    }
    85	    case LOOP_EVENT.GATE_ITERATION: {
    86	      const gate = String(ev.gate);
    87	      const current = state.iterations?.[gate] ?? 0;
    88	      // The 6th attempt is REFUSED: the counter stays at the cap and the run
    89	      // escalates with a record naming the gate — never a 6th run.
    90	      if (current >= GATE_ITERATION_CAP) {
    91	        return { ...state, status: LOOP_STATUS.ESCALATED, escalation: { gate, iteration: current } };
    92	      }
    93	      return { ...state, iterations: { ...state.iterations, [gate]: current + 1 } };
    94	    }
    95	    case LOOP_EVENT.PARK:
    96	      return { ...state, status: LOOP_STATUS.PARKED, parkReason: ev.reason ?? null };
    97	    case LOOP_EVENT.RESUME:
    98	      // Only a PARK is resumable; an escalation is an operator decision.
    99	      if (state.status !== LOOP_STATUS.PARKED) return state;
   100	      return { ...state, status: LOOP_STATUS.RUNNING, parkReason: null };
   101	    case LOOP_EVENT.SMOKE_AWAIT:
   102	      return { ...state, status: LOOP_STATUS.AWAITING_SMOKE_APPROVAL };
   103	    case LOOP_EVENT.SMOKE_APPROVE: {
   104	      // Guarded transition: only meaningful while awaiting, and only with the
   105	      // caller's verifySmokeToken result stamped verified === true. A missing
   106	      // or false `verified` is unverified — it never resumes the run.
   107	      if (state.status !== LOOP_STATUS.AWAITING_SMOKE_APPROVAL) return state;
   108	      if (ev.verified !== true) return state;
   109	      return { ...state, status: LOOP_STATUS.RUNNING, smokeApproval: { token: ev.token, at: ev.ts ?? null } };
   110	    }
   111	    default:
   112	      return state;
   113	  }
   114	}
   115	
   116	/**
   117	 * Atomic snapshot write (tmp + rename under .handoff/loop).
   118	 * @param {string} root @param {any} state @param {any} io
   119	 */
   120	export async function writeLoopState(root, state, io) {
   121	  const p = loopPaths(root);
   122	  ensureDir(io.fs, p.dir);
   123	  atomicWriteJson(io.fs, p.state, state);
   124	}

   126	/**
   127	 * Append one journal event; allocates the next seq past
   128	 * max(snapshot.journalSeq, journal tail) unless the entry carries one.
   129	 * @param {string} root @param {any} ev @param {any} io
   130	 * @returns {Promise<number>} the persisted seq
   131	 */
   132	export async function appendLoopEvent(root, ev, io) {
   133	  const p = loopPaths(root);
   134	  ensureDir(io.fs, p.dir);
   135	  let seq = ev.seq;
   136	  if (typeof seq !== 'number') {
   137	    const snap = safeReadJson(io.fs, p.state);
   138	    const snapSeq = snap.ok && typeof snap.value?.journalSeq === 'number' ? snap.value.journalSeq : 0;
   139	    let tailSeq = 0;
   140	    if (io.fs.existsSync(p.journal)) {
   141	      for (const e of readAllTolerant(io.fs, p.journal).entries) {
   142	        if (typeof e.seq === 'number' && e.seq > tailSeq) tailSeq = e.seq;
   143	      }
   144	    }
   145	    seq = Math.max(snapSeq, tailSeq) + 1;
   146	  }
   147	  const ts = typeof ev.ts === 'string' ? ev.ts : io.now();
   148	  const entry = {
   149	    ...ev,
   150	    seq,
   151	    ts,
   152	    dedupeKey: typeof ev.dedupeKey === 'string' && ev.dedupeKey.length > 0 ? ev.dedupeKey : dedupeKey({ seq, ts, type: ev.type, gate: ev.gate ?? null }),
   153	  };
   154	  appendEntry(io.fs, p.journal, entry);
   155	  return seq;
   156	}
   157	
   158	/**
   159	 * Load = snapshot + torn-tail-tolerant replay of journal events PAST the
   160	 * snapshot's seq. Duplicate seqs/dedupeKeys apply exactly once, so a
   161	 * supervisor-death recovery never re-runs a completed iteration.
   162	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io
   163	 * @returns {Promise<{state: any, warnings: string[]}>}
   164	 */
   165	export async function loadLoopState(root, io) {
   166	  const p = loopPaths(root);
   167	  /** @type {string[]} */
   168	  const warnings = [];
   169	  const snap = safeReadJson(io.fs, p.state);
   170	  if (!snap.ok) return { state: null, warnings: ['no loop state snapshot found'] };
   171	  let state = snap.value;
   172	  const baseSeq = typeof state.journalSeq === 'number' ? state.journalSeq : 0;
   173	
   174	  if (io.fs.existsSync(p.journal)) {
   175	    const { entries, warnings: jw } = readAllTolerant(io.fs, p.journal);
   176	    for (const w of jw ?? []) warnings.push(`journal: ${w.kind ?? 'warning'} at line ${w.line ?? '?'}`);
   177	    const applied = new Set();
   178	    let maxSeq = baseSeq;
   179	    for (const e of entries) {
   180	      const seq = typeof e.seq === 'number' ? e.seq : null;
   181	      if (seq !== null && seq <= baseSeq) continue; // already folded into the snapshot
   182	      const key = e.dedupeKey ?? (seq !== null ? `seq:${seq}` : null);
   183	      if (key !== null && applied.has(key)) continue; // replayed duplicate — apply once
   184	      if (seq !== null && applied.has(`seq:${seq}`)) continue;
   185	      state = applyLoopEvent(state, e);
   186	      if (key !== null) applied.add(key);
   187	      if (seq !== null) {
   188	        applied.add(`seq:${seq}`);
   189	        if (seq > maxSeq) maxSeq = seq;
   190	      }
   191	    }
   192	    state = { ...state, journalSeq: maxSeq };
   193	  }
   194	  return { state, warnings };
   195	}

   197	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   198	// Smoke-approval token — a STRUCTURED digest over the six bound inputs, so a
   199	// stale approval is refused NAMING what moved (mirrors the receive receipt
   200	// token's driftedInputs discipline).
   201	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   202	
   203	const SMOKE_TOKEN_PREFIX = 'smk1';
   204	const SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS = /** @type {const} */ ([
   205	  'stateDigest',
   206	  'smokeCmd',
   207	  'smokeOutputDigest',
   208	  'gitHead',
   209	  'gitContentDigest',
   210	  'childAssignment',
   211	]);
   212	
   213	/**
   214	 * Deterministic structured token. Per-field digests keep field boundaries
   215	 * (no concatenation collisions) and let verification name drifted inputs.
   216	 * Missing bound fields throw — a token over partial inputs is meaningless.
   217	 * @param {Record<string, string>} inputs
   218	 * @returns {string}
   219	 */
   220	export function smokeApprovalToken(inputs) {
   221	  for (const f of SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS) {
   222	    if (typeof inputs?.[f] !== 'string') throw new Error(`smoke approval token: required input '${f}' is missing`);
   223	  }
   224	  return `${SMOKE_TOKEN_PREFIX}.` + SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS.map((f) => dedupeKey(inputs[f]).slice(0, 10)).join('.');
   225	}
   226	
   227	/**
   228	 * Recompute against current inputs; positional comparison names every
   229	 * drifted input. Never throws — partial current inputs simply cannot verify.
   230	 * @param {string} presented @param {Record<string, string>} inputs
   231	 * @returns {{ok: true} | {ok: false, driftedInputs: string[]}}
   232	 */
   233	export function verifySmokeToken(presented, inputs) {
   234	  /** @type {string} */
   235	  let current;
   236	  try {
   237	    current = smokeApprovalToken(inputs);
   238	  } catch {
   239	    return { ok: false, driftedInputs: SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS.filter((f) => typeof inputs?.[f] !== 'string') };
   240	  }
   241	  if (presented === current) return { ok: true };
   242	  const a = String(presented ?? '').split('.');
   243	  const b = current.split('.');
   244	  /** @type {string[]} */
   245	  const drifted = [];
   246	  SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS.forEach((f, i) => {
   247	    if (a[i + 1] !== b[i + 1]) drifted.push(f);
   248	  });
   249	  return { ok: false, driftedInputs: drifted.length > 0 ? drifted : [...SMOKE_TOKEN_FIELDS] };
   250	}

   426	    assert.equal(code, 2, 'a valueless --approve-smoke must not silently run unapproved');
   427	  });
   428

    13

    15	
    16	/**
    17	 * The scaffold `baton loop init` writes. Phase ids are progress labels;

    48	/**
    49	 * Validate a loop spec against the role matrix. Reports EVERY problem at
    50	 * once (each error names its offender) so a spec author fixes one round, not
    51	 * one field per run. Valid specs are returned normalized: caller-provided
    52	 * fields are preserved verbatim; only ABSENT constraints/budgets/smoke are
    53	 * filled with defaults.
    54	 * @param {any} spec
    55	 * @param {any} config the parsed baton.config.json (roles are checked against it)
    56	 * @returns {{ok: true, spec: any} | {ok: false, errors: string[]}}
    57	 */
    58	export function validateLoopSpec(spec, config) {
    59	  /** @type {string[]} */
    60	  const errors = [];
    61	  const s = spec ?? {};
    62	
    63	  if (s.schema !== LOOP_SCHEMA) errors.push(`schema must be '${LOOP_SCHEMA}' (got ${JSON.stringify(s.schema)})`);
    64	  if (typeof s.goal !== 'string' || s.goal.length === 0) errors.push('goal must be a non-empty string');
    65	
    66	  let constraints = s.constraints;
    67	  if (constraints === undefined) constraints = [];
    68	  if (!Array.isArray(constraints)) {
    69	    errors.push('constraints must be an array of strings');
    70	  } else {
    71	    constraints.forEach((c, i) => {
    72	      if (typeof c !== 'string') errors.push(`constraints[${i}] must be a string (got ${JSON.stringify(c)})`);
    73	    });
    74	  }
    75	
    76	  const roles = config?.roles ?? {};
    77	  if (!Array.isArray(s.phases) || s.phases.length === 0) {
    78	    errors.push('phases must be a non-empty array of {id, role}');
    79	  } else {
    80	    s.phases.forEach((/** @type {any} */ p, /** @type {number} */ i) => {
    81	      if (typeof p?.id !== 'string' || p.id.length === 0) errors.push(`phases[${i}] is missing an id (a non-empty progress label)`);
    82	      if (typeof p?.role !== 'string' || p.role.length === 0) {
    83	        errors.push(`phases[${i}] is missing a role (a baton.config.json role ID)`);
    84	      } else if (!(p.role in roles)) {
    85	        errors.push(`phases[${i}]: unknown role '${p.role}' — add it to baton.config.json roles or fix the reference`);
    86	      }
    87	    });
    88	  }
    89	
    90	  let budgets = s.budgets;
    91	  if (budgets === undefined) {
    92	    budgets = { ...DEFAULT_BUDGETS };
    93	  } else if (typeof budgets !== 'object' || budgets === null) {
    94	    errors.push('budgets must be an object');
    95	  } else {
    96	    const cap = budgets.iterationCap;
    97	    if (typeof cap !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(cap) || cap < 1 || cap > ITERATION_CAP_MAX) {
    98	      errors.push(`budgets.iterationCap must be a number between 1 and ${ITERATION_CAP_MAX} (the 5-iteration cap is a hard invariant; got ${JSON.stringify(cap)})`);
    99	    }
   100	    for (const field of ['perRoleTimeoutMin', 'maxChildrenPerPhase']) {
   101	      const v = budgets[field];
   102	      if (typeof v !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(v) || v <= 0) {
   103	        errors.push(`budgets.${field} must be a positive number (got ${JSON.stringify(v)})`);
   104	      }
   105	    }
   106	  }
   107	
   108	  let smoke = s.smoke;
   109	  if (smoke === undefined) {
   110	    smoke = { cmd: null, expect: null };
   111	  } else if (typeof smoke !== 'object' || smoke === null) {
   112	    errors.push('smoke must be an object ({cmd, expect}, each a string or null)');
   113	  } else {
   114	    if (!(smoke.cmd === null || typeof smoke.cmd === 'string')) errors.push(`smoke.cmd must be a string or null (got ${JSON.stringify(smoke.cmd)})`);
   115	    if (!(smoke.expect === null || typeof smoke.expect === 'string')) errors.push(`smoke.expect must be a string or null (got ${JSON.stringify(smoke.expect)})`);
   116	  }
   117	
   118	  if (errors.length > 0) return { ok: false, errors };
   119	  return { ok: true, spec: { ...s, constraints, budgets, smoke } };
   120	}

     5	// Flags that consume a value — needed to split positionals from flag tokens
     6	// without mistaking a flag's value for a positional. Keep in sync with the
     7	// strict spec below plus the implied common string flag (--root).
     8	const STRING_FLAGS = new Set(['root']);
     9	
    10	/**
    11	 * `baton loop <subcommand>` — the Layer-2 goal-loop surface. v1 subcommands:
    12	 * `init "<goal>"` (scaffold loop.json; two-phase, idempotent, dry-run-able).
    13	 * Supervisor-side by design: the BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD guard deliberately
    14	 * does NOT apply here.
    15	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
    16	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
    17	 */
    18	export async function cmdLoop(args, io) {
    19	  /** @type {string[]} */
    20	  const positionals = [];
    21	  /** @type {string[]} */
    22	  const flagTokens = [];
    23	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
    24	    const a = args[i];
    25	    if (typeof a === 'string' && a.startsWith('--')) {
    26	      flagTokens.push(a);
    27	      if (STRING_FLAGS.has(a.slice(2)) && i + 1 < args.length) {
    28	        i += 1;
    29	        flagTokens.push(args[i]);
    30	      }
    31	    } else {
    32	      positionals.push(a);
    33	    }
    34	  }
    35	
    36	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(flagTokens, { 'dry-run': 'boolean' });
    37	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'loop', parsed.error);
    38	  const flags = parsed.flags;
    39	
    40	  const sub = positionals[0];
    41	  if (sub === undefined) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', 'a subcommand is required — try: baton loop init "<goal>"');
    42	  if (sub !== 'init') return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `unknown subcommand '${sub}' (supported: init)`);
    43	
    44	  const goal = positionals[1];
    45	  if (goal === undefined) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', 'loop init requires a goal — baton loop init "<goal>"');
    46	  if (positionals.length > 2) return usageError(io, flags, 'loop', `unexpected argument '${positionals[2]}'`);
    47	
    48	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
    49	  const path = `${root}/loop.json`;
    50	
    51	  const finish = (/** @type {any} */ data, /** @type {string} */ human) => {
    52	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data });
    53	    else io.stdout.write(`${human}\n`);
    54	    return 0;
    55	  };
    56	
    57	  // Idempotent: an existing spec is the user's — never overwritten.
    58	  if (io.fs.existsSync(path)) {
    59	    return finish({ created: false, path }, `baton loop init: ${path} already exists — left untouched`);
    60	  }
    61	  if (flags['dry-run'] === true) {
    62	    return finish(
    63	      { created: false, path, dryRun: true },
    64	      `baton loop init (dry-run): would write ${path} — the default baton/loop@1 spec with goal "${goal}"`,
    65	    );
    66	  }
    67	  ensureDir(io.fs, root);
    68	  atomicWriteJson(io.fs, path, defaultLoopSpec(goal));
    69	  return finish({ created: true, path }, `baton loop init: wrote ${path} (goal "${goal}") — edit constraints/smoke, then run baton loop run`);
    70	}

     1	// Fake `io` object matching the injected-io contract from docs/design/core.md:
     2	// { cwd, env, stdin, stdout, stderr, fs, execFile, now }. Backed by memfs.
     3	// stdout/stderr collect writes; io.stdoutText()/io.stderrText() flatten them.
     4	// now() returns a settable ISO string (io.setNow). execFile resolves from an
     5	// execResults map keyed by the joined command string.
     6	//
     7	// Wave-B2 additions (bundle lock layer) — all optional, defaulted, and purely
     8	// additive so no prior consumer is affected:
     9	//   host / pid / startTime  — the process-identity facts the lock model writes
    10	//     into owner.json and compares on contention (see plan §Concurrency, Lock
    11	//     model iterations 3+4).
    12	//   processAlive(pid, startTime) — the "provably dead" oracle. Default: only
    13	//     THIS io's own {pid, startTime} is alive; every other descriptor reads as
    14	//     dead. Override per test to model a live foreign owner or a pid/start-time
    15	//     mismatch (reused pid).
    16	//   newFencingToken() — the injected per-acquisition token source. Deterministic
    17	//     monotonic counter ("tok-1", "tok-2", …), matching the injected-io
    18	//     discipline already used for now()/execFile so lock acquisition is
    19	//     reproducible in tests rather than drawing from Math.random.
    20	
    21	import { makeMemfs } from './memfs.mjs';
    22	
    23	export function makeIo({
    24	  files = {},
    25	  env = {},
    26	  stdin = '',
    27	  execResults = {},
    28	  now = '2026-07-11T00:00:00.000Z',
    29	  host = 'host-A',
    30	  pid = 4242,
    31	  startTime = 111000,
    32	  processAlive = null,
    33	  fencingSeed = 1,
    34	  execPath = process.execPath,
    35	} = {}) {
    36	  const { fs, files: filesSnapshot } = makeMemfs(files);
    37	  const outChunks = [];
    38	  const errChunks = [];
    39	  let currentNow = now;
    40	  let tokenCounter = fencingSeed - 1;
    41	  const defaultAlive = (p, s) => p === pid && s === startTime;
    42	
    43	  const stdout = { write: (s) => { outChunks.push(String(s)); return true; } };
    44	  const stderr = { write: (s) => { errChunks.push(String(s)); return true; } };
    45	
    46	  const execFile = (cmd, args = [], /* opts */ _opts = {}) => {
    47	    const key = [cmd, ...(Array.isArray(args) ? args : [])].join(' ');
    48	    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    49	      if (!(key in execResults)) {
    50	        const e = new Error(`spawn ${cmd} ENOENT`);
    51	        e.code = 'ENOENT';
    52	        return reject(e);
    53	      }
    54	      const r = execResults[key];
    55	      const code = r.code ?? 0;
    56	      const out = r.stdout ?? '';
    57	      const err = r.stderr ?? '';
    58	      if (code !== 0) {
    59	        // util.promisify(execFile) rejects on nonzero exit; error carries code + streams.
    60	        const e = new Error(`Command failed: ${key}`);
    61	        e.code = code;
    62	        e.stdout = out;
    63	        e.stderr = err;
    64	        return reject(e);
    65	      }
    66	      resolve({ stdout: out, stderr: err });
    67	    });
    68	  };
    69	
    70	  return {
    71	    cwd: '/repo',
    72	    env,
    73	    stdin,
    74	    stdout,
    75	    stderr,
    76	    fs,
    77	    execFile,
    78	    now: () => currentNow,
    79	    setNow: (iso) => { currentNow = iso; },
    80	    execPath,
    81	    host,
    82	    pid,
    83	    startTime,
    84	    processAlive: processAlive || defaultAlive,
    85	    // Tiny retry budget: unit tests exercising live-lock refusal stay fast
    86	    // while the retry code path itself still runs (production default: 120x25ms).
    87	    lockRetry: { attempts: 2, delayMs: 2 },
    88	    newFencingToken: () => `tok-${++tokenCounter}`,
    89	    stdoutText: () => outChunks.join(''),
    90	    stderrText: () => errChunks.join(''),
    91	    files: filesSnapshot,
    92	  };
    93	}

     1	/**
     2	 * Loop failover orchestration — what the supervisor does when a child dies.
     3	 * Classifies the death via the signature table, then takes exactly one path:
     4	 * retry-once-then-park (generic failures), entry-level re-resolve
     5	 * (model-unavailable — the platform survives its dead model), or the
     6	 * usage-limit transaction: checkpoint the loop position INTO the bundle,
     7	 * seal, and receive onto the resolver's pick with one bounded stale retry.
     8	 * Writes NOTHING under .handoff/loop/ — the supervisor applies the returned
     9	 * decision to loop state afterward. Plan:
    10	 * docs/plans/2026-07-18-goal-loop-worktree-pipeline.md §"Limit failover" +
    11	 * §"Model-level failover".
    12	 */
    13	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
    14	import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
    15	import { loadSignatures } from '../detect/signatures.mjs';
    16	import { classify } from '../detect/classifier.mjs';
    17	import { resolveRoles } from '../roles/resolve.mjs';
    18	import { loadBundle } from '../bundle/store.mjs';
    19	import { snapshot as gitSnapshot } from '../git/snapshot.mjs';
    20	import { prepare, commit } from '../receive/txn.mjs';
    21	import { cmdCheckpoint } from '../commands/checkpoint.mjs';
    22	import { cmdFinalize } from '../commands/finalize.mjs';
    23	
    24	const BUILTIN_SIGNATURES = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..', 'data', 'signatures.v1.json');
    25	
    26	/**
    27	 * @param {{
    28	 *   root: string, io: any, config: any, role: string,
    29	 *   assignment: {platform: string, role?: string, model: string, effort?: string | null, mode?: string},
    30	 *   transcript: string, exitCode: number, sessionHint: string,
    31	 *   probes?: any, avoid?: string[], avoidEntries?: Array<{platform: string, model: string}>,
    32	 *   attempt: number, loopState?: any, degradedOpen?: boolean,
    33	 * }} input
    34	 * @returns {Promise<
    35	 *   | {action: 'retry', class: string, attempt: number}
    36	 *   | {action: 'park', class: string, reason: string, resumeAt?: string}
    37	 *   | {action: 'relaunch', class: string, assignment: any, avoidEntries?: any[], prompt?: string}
    38	 * >}
    39	 */
    40	export async function runFailover(input) {
    41	  const { root, io, config, role, assignment, sessionHint } = input;
    42	  const avoid = input.avoid ?? [];
    43	  const avoidEntries = input.avoidEntries ?? [];
    44	
    45	  // Classification is TABLE-driven — the same loader/classifier as `baton
    46	  // detect`, so overlay/fixture signatures are honored, never hardcoded.
    47	  const table = loadSignatures({ builtinPath: BUILTIN_SIGNATURES }, io);
    48	  const verdict = classify({ text: input.transcript, exitCode: input.exitCode, platform: assignment.platform, table });
    49	
    50	  // Model-level failure: the platform is fine, one model is dead. Avoid the
    51	  // exact {platform, model} tuple and re-resolve — no seal, no receive.
    52	  if (verdict.class === 'model-unavailable') {
    53	    const nextAvoidEntries = [...avoidEntries, { platform: assignment.platform, model: assignment.model }];
    54	    const resolved = resolveRoles({ config, to: assignment.platform, avoid, avoidEntries: nextAvoidEntries, probes: input.probes ?? null });
    55	    const next = resolved.assignments[role];
    56	    if (!next || next.mode === 'unavailable') {
    57	      return { action: 'park', class: verdict.class, reason: `no eligible chain entry left for role '${role}' after avoiding ${assignment.platform}/${assignment.model}` };
    58	    }
    59	    return { action: 'relaunch', class: verdict.class, assignment: next, avoidEntries: nextAvoidEntries };
    60	  }
    61	
    62	  // Anything that is not a usage-limit death is a child failure, not a
    63	  // platform death: retry once, then park. Never a seal or receive.
    64	  if (verdict.class !== 'usage-limit') {
    65	    if (input.attempt <= 1) return { action: 'retry', class: verdict.class, attempt: input.attempt };
    66	    return { action: 'park', class: verdict.class, reason: `child failed twice (${verdict.class}) — parked for operator review` };
    67	  }
    68	
    69	  // ---- Usage-limit: the exact transaction (plan steps 3–8). ----------------
    70	  const { bundle } = loadBundle(root, io);
    71	  const originPlatform = bundle?.origin?.platform ?? assignment.platform;
    72	
    73	  // (3) Checkpoint the loop position INTO the bundle under the supervisor
    74	  // session BEFORE any seal, so the frozen seal carries it.
    75	  if (input.loopState !== undefined) {
    76	    const checkpointIo = {
    77	      ...io,
    78	      stdin: JSON.stringify({
    79	        schema: 'baton/event@1',
    80	        events: [{ type: 'decision', payload: { summary: `loop position at limit death: ${JSON.stringify(input.loopState)}` } }],
    81	      }),
    82	    };
    83	    await cmdCheckpoint(['--platform', originPlatform, '--session', sessionHint, '--root', root], checkpointIo);
    84	  }
    85	
    86	  // (4) Seal — unless the caller knows a clean seal is impossible
    87	  // (degradedOpen: a prior death left the bundle unsealed; receive's
    88	  // degraded-open path compensates), or the bundle is already sealed.
    89	  const alreadySealed = bundle?.handoff?.status === 'sealed';
    90	  if (input.degradedOpen !== true && !alreadySealed) {
    91	    await cmdFinalize(['--reason', 'usage-limit death during a supervised loop run', '--reason-class', 'usage-limit', '--root', root], io);
    92	  }
    93	
    94	  // (7, ordered before receive because receive needs the target) — resolver
    95	  // pick with the dead origin platform avoided.
    96	  const relaunchAvoid = avoid.includes(assignment.platform) ? avoid : [...avoid, assignment.platform];
    97	  const resolved = resolveRoles({ config, to: assignment.platform, avoid: relaunchAvoid, avoidEntries, probes: input.probes ?? null });
    98	  const target = resolved.assignments[role];
    99	  if (!target || target.mode === 'unavailable') {
   100	    return {
   101	      action: 'park',
   102	      class: verdict.class,
   103	      reason: `every platform is avoided or unavailable for role '${role}' — parked with a resume hint`,
   104	      ...(verdict.resetHint ? { resumeAt: verdict.resetHint } : {}),
   105	    };
   106	  }
   107	
   108	  // (5–6) Receive prepare+commit back-to-back with IDENTICAL intake and the
   109	  // supervisor session hint. Git is re-derived fresh for each phase (exactly
   110	  // as the CLI does), so real drift inside the window stales the token; ONE
   111	  // automatic re-prepare retry, then park. No .handoff/loop writes anywhere.
   112	  const receiveOpts = (/** @type {any} */ git) => ({
   113	    platform: target.platform,
   114	    origin: 'unknown', // defaults from the sealed bundle's recorded origin
   115	    reason: 'unspecified', // defaults from the sealed reason
   116	    reasonClass: 'usage-limit',
   117	    gitSnapshot: git,
   118	    probes: input.probes ?? null,
   119	    sessionHint,
   120	    sessionUnstable: false,
   121	  });
   122	
   123	  /** @type {string} */
   124	  let prompt = '';
   125	  let lastError = null;
   126	  for (let window = 1; window <= 2; window += 1) {
   127	    const prepGit = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   128	    const prepared = prepare(root, receiveOpts(prepGit), io);
   129	    prompt = prepared.prompt;
   130	    const commitGit = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   131	    try {
   132	      commit(root, prepared.token, receiveOpts(commitGit), io);
   133	      lastError = null;
   134	      break;
   135	    } catch (err) {
   136	      lastError = err;
   137	    }
   138	  }
   139	  if (lastError !== null) {
   140	    const msg = /** @type {any} */ (lastError)?.message ?? String(lastError);
   141	    return { action: 'park', class: verdict.class, reason: `receive commit stayed stale after one re-prepare retry — ${msg}` };
   142	  }
   143	
   144	  // (8) Relaunch on the adopted platform with the resume prompt.
   145	  return {
   146	    action: 'relaunch',
   147	    class: verdict.class,
   148	    assignment: target,
   149	    avoidEntries,
   150	    prompt,
   151	  };
   152	}

   141	// A git execFile whose HEAD is chosen per rev-parse-HEAD call (the drift seam),
   142	// and which counts those calls so a test can pin the exact number of
   143	// prepare->commit windows. gitSnapshot reads clean status/diffs.
   144	function gitExec(headForCall) {
   145	  let headCalls = 0;
   146	  const fn = (/** @type {string} */ cmd, /** @type {string[]} */ args = []) => {
   147	    if (cmd !== 'git') return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('spawn ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }));
   148	    const key = args.join(' ');
   149	    if (key === 'rev-parse HEAD') {
   150	      headCalls += 1;
   151	      return Promise.resolve({ stdout: headForCall(headCalls) + '\n', stderr: '' });
   152	    }
   153	    const out = key === 'rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD' ? 'main' : '';
   154	    return Promise.resolve({ stdout: out + '\n', stderr: '' });
   155	  };
   156	  fn.headCalls = () => headCalls;
   157	  return fn;
   158	}

   160	// Spy every write touching .handoff/loop.
   161	function spyLoopWrites(io) {
   162	  const writes = /** @type {string[]} */ ([]);
   163	  const note = (/** @type {any} */ p) => { if (typeof p === 'string' && p.startsWith('/repo/.handoff/loop')) writes.push(p); };
   164	  for (const m of ['writeFileSync', 'appendFileSync', 'mkdirSync', 'unlinkSync', 'rmSync']) {
   165	    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
   166	    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ p, /** @type {any} */ a) => { note(p); return real(p, a); };
   167	  }
   168	  for (const m of ['renameSync', 'copyFileSync']) {
   169	    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
   170	    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ from, /** @type {any} */ to) => { note(from); note(to); return real(from, to); };
   171	  }
   172	  return writes;
   173	}

   175	const historyFreezes = (io) => {
   176	  const dir = bundlePaths('/repo').historyDir;
   177	  if (!io.fs.existsSync(dir)) return [];
   178	  // Parse ONLY snapshot freezes (.json). rotateJournalIn also writes .ndjson
   179	  // journal freezes here — legitimately empty or multi-line — which are not JSON.
   180	  return io.fs
   181	    .readdirSync(dir)
   182	    .filter((/** @type {string} */ n) => n.endsWith('.json'))
   183	    .map((/** @type {string} */ n) => ({ name: n, data: JSON.parse(io.fs.readFileSync(`${dir}/${n}`, 'utf8')) }));
   184	};

   208	  it('other-error on the FIRST attempt -> {action:retry}', async () => {
   209	    const { runFailover } = M();
   210	    const io = makeRepoIo();
   211	    const d = await runFailover(usageLimitInput(io, { transcript: 'Error: build failed with 3 errors', exitCode: 1, attempt: 1 }));
   212	    assert.equal(d.class, 'other-error');
   213	    assert.equal(d.action, 'retry', 'a generic failure retries once');
   214	  });
   215	
   216	  it('other-error on the SECOND attempt -> {action:park} (retry-once-then-park)', async () => {
   217	    const { runFailover } = M();
   218	    const io = makeRepoIo();
   219	    const d = await runFailover(usageLimitInput(io, { transcript: 'Error: build failed', exitCode: 1, attempt: 2 }));
   220	    assert.equal(d.class, 'other-error');
   221	    assert.equal(d.action, 'park', 'a second consecutive generic failure parks');
   222	    assert.ok(typeof d.reason === 'string' && d.reason.length > 0, 'the park records a reason');
   223	  });

   229	    const live = loadBundle('/repo', io).bundle;
   230	    assert.equal(live.generation, 1, 'no generation opened for a non-limit failure');
   231	    assert.equal(historyFreezes(io).length, 0, 'no seal/receive freeze for a non-limit failure');
   232	  });

    69	### `baton loop` (Layer 2)
    70	
    71	- `baton loop init <goal>` — scaffold spec + plan template; idempotent,
    72	  dry-run-able, same two-phase plan/apply discipline as `baton init`.
    73	- `baton loop run [--approve-smoke <token>]` — the state machine. State lives
    74	  in gitignored `.handoff/loop/state.json` + `journal.ndjson` (same atomic
    75	  write + journal replay machinery as the bundle; loop position is also
    76	  checkpointed into the handoff bundle so a limit death carries it).
    77	
    78	### Root + ownership discipline (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 2)
    79	
    80	One authoritative root: the MAIN repo root where `loop.json` lives. The
    81	supervisor is the SOLE writer of `.handoff/loop/` and of the main root's
    82	handoff bundle; every supervisor-driven baton invocation passes explicit
    83	`--root <mainRoot>` and a supervisor-owned stable session hint
    84	(`--session loop-<runId>` — a NEW flag added to `checkpoint`; `receive`
    85	already has it), so the bundle has exactly one stable owner.
    86	
    87	**Child-hook policy (Gate-1 iteration 2, finding 1; iteration 3,
    88	finding 1)** — children never touch OR read any bundle, by construction: the
    89	supervisor sets `BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD=1` in every child's environment, and
    90	EVERY baton hook command — the hook entrypoints, `baton checkpoint`, and
    91	`baton session-start` (which would otherwise read the bundle and inject
    92	pending-handoff resume context into the child) — quietly no-ops (exit 0,
    93	empty output) when it is set. This covers
    94	Layer-2 children running in the MAIN root (where root discovery would
    95	otherwise find the supervisor-owned bundle and the foreign-session guard
    96	would reject their stable hints) and pipeline children in worktrees alike;
    97	narrative checkpointing for supervised work is the supervisor's job, driven
    98	by parsed child results. Contract tests: (a) Layer-2 — two concurrent
    99	main-root children with distinct stable session hints and live hooks →
   100	zero bundle mutations, zero foreign-session rejections, supervisor
   101	`--session` checkpoints land; (b) pipeline — same from two worktrees while
   102	the supervisor writes loop state.
   103	- Each role invocation is a headless child under the supervisor:
   104	  - claude-code roles: `claude -p "<role prompt>" --permission-mode
   105	    acceptEdits --allowedTools ...` (allowlist per role: reviewers read-only).
   106	  - codex roles: `codex exec -C <root> -s <sandbox> --model <m> -c
   107	    model_reasoning_effort=<e> "<prompt>" </dev/null` (stdin closed — the
   108	    stdin-hang class is a known field failure).
   109	  - Verdict contract: children end with the structured tail
   110	    (`VERDICT: APPROVED|APPROVED_WITH_NOTES|BLOCKED` + FINDINGS) already used
   111	    by every review gate; the supervisor parses exactly that.
   112	
   113	### Child supervision contract (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 7)
   114	
   115	`children.mjs` owns the full child lifecycle, not just argv assembly:
   116	
   117	- Spawn detached in its OWN process group; stdin closed at spawn (the
   118	  codex-exec stdin-hang class); per-role timeout → SIGTERM to the group, 10 s
   119	  grace, then SIGKILL to the group (no zombie grandchildren; reap verified in
   120	  tests with a child that forks a sleeper).
   121	- Full child output streams to `.handoff/loop/children/<child-id>.log` with a
   122	  byte cap (head preserved, middle truncated with a marker — the verdict tail
   123	  is at the END so the tail is never truncated).
   124	- **Verdict parsing is region-bounded (prompt-echo defense)**: only the
   125	  child's FINAL message region is parsed — claude-code children run with a
   126	  structured output format and the parser reads the result field; codex
   127	  children are parsed strictly AFTER the last `tokens used` marker. The
   128	  prompt region (which quotes `VERDICT:` in its instructions) is never
   129	  scanned. Multiple tails in the final region → the LAST one wins.
   130	- An unparseable, absent, or truncated verdict is BLOCKED-with-escalation,
   131	  never APPROVED; a child that exits after making edits but before a verdict
   132	  parks the subtask with its worktree preserved for inspection.
   133	- A generic nonzero exit classifies as `other-error` (existing classifier
   134	  rule) → the loop retries once, then parks; it NEVER triggers limit failover
   135	  without limit-specific evidence.
   136	- Fixture-driven tests: prompt echo, multiple verdict tails, truncated
   137	  transcript, timeout kill/reap, zombie grandchild, non-limit nonzero exit.
   138	
   139	### Supervisor lifetime and recovery (Gate-1 iteration 2, finding 5)
   140	
   141	"Survives the operator's session ending" is a defined mechanism, not a hope:
   142	
   143	- `baton loop run` is FOREGROUND by default. `--detach` re-launches the
   144	  supervisor in its own session (`setsid`), output to
   145	  `.handoff/loop/supervisor.log`, and returns.
   146	- A run lock `.handoff/loop/supervisor.lock` carries {pid, process
   147	  start-time, host, runId} — the same provably-dead machinery as the
   148	  Layer-1 bundle lock. A second `loop run` against a LIVE supervisor is
   149	  refused; against a provably-dead one it recovers.
   150	- The state machine is journal-replayable: recovery replays
   151	  `journal.ndjson`, marks any in-flight child of the dead supervisor as
   152	  interrupted (its process group is gone or killed on adoption), and either
   153	  continues from the last completed step or parks with an escalation note —
   154	  never re-runs a completed gate iteration.
   155	- Acceptance adds a supervisor-death test: kill the supervisor (and its
   156	  launching session) mid-subtask → a fresh `loop run` recovers via the
   157	  journal and continues or parks; no orphaned children survive (process
   158	  groups reaped on adoption).
   159	
   160	- **Smoke gate (staleness-proof — Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 8; TDD order —
   161	  iteration 2, finding 2)**: after gate-1, the smoke slice is built as a TDD
   162	  mini-cycle (test-author writes the failing smoke assertion → test-verifier
   163	  approves it → implementer writes only enough to pass it — the repo TDD
   164	  contract applies to the slice, not just to subtasks); the supervisor then
   165	  runs `smoke.cmd`, records output, and STOPS, writing
   166	  `.handoff/loop/SMOKE-REVIEW.md` plus `smoke-approval.json` containing an
   167	  approval token = digest over {loop-state digest, smoke.cmd, output digest,
   168	  HEAD, content-sensitive git digest (existing snapshot machinery), child
   169	  assignment}. Resuming requires `baton loop run --approve-smoke <token>`;
   170	  the supervisor recomputes the digest first and REFUSES a drifted token
   171	  (anything changed since the human looked) — it parks for a fresh smoke run
   172	  instead. No full-run budget is spent before a valid approval.
   173	- **Limit failover (the baton integration — Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 3)**:
   174	  an exact transaction, not a loose chain. On child death: (1) reap the
   175	  process group and freeze the transcript; (2) classify via `baton detect`;
   176	  non-limit → the retry/park path above. On a limit classification:
   177	  (3) checkpoint the loop position INTO THE BUNDLE (supervisor
   178	  `checkpoint --session loop-<runId>`) so the seal carries it and the receipt
   179	  token binds it; (4) seal via `finalize --reason-class usage-limit --root
   180	  <mainRoot>` (an already-dead/unsealed bundle takes the degraded-open path
   181	  receive already supports); (5) refresh probes; (6) `receive --prepare` then
   182	  `--commit` back-to-back with IDENTICAL intake flags, the supervisor session
   183	  hint, and the same explicit root, with NO intervening writes; (7) resolver
   184	  output (with the dead entry avoided) picks the relaunch platform+model;
   185	  (8) relaunch the child with the resume prompt. A stale-token rejection
   186	  triggers ONE automatic re-prepare/commit retry; a second failure parks.
   187	  Between prepare and commit the failover holds the loop transaction lock and
   188	  writes NOTHING — `.handoff/loop/` writes are not token-bound inputs, so
   189	  this is enforced by construction and ASSERTED in tests (fs spy: zero
   190	  `.handoff/loop/` writes inside the window), not assumed. Drift-rejection
   191	  tests inject the inputs the token actually binds: git change and probe
   192	  refresh between prepare and commit → stale-token → one retry path. Plus:
   193	  open-bundle (unsealed) limit death; the full seal→receive→relaunch happy
   194	  path.
   195	- **Model-level failover (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 4)**: the resolver
   196	  gains entry-level avoidance — `avoidEntries: [{platform, model}]` alongside
   197	  the existing platform-level `avoid[]` — and the classifier gains a
   198	  `model-unavailable` signature class (distinct from usage-limit; seeded with
   199	  the verified account-tier rejection string). A model rejected at spawn adds
   200	  its {platform, model} entry to avoidEntries and re-resolves: other models
   201	  on the SAME platform remain selectable. Named test: first chain entry
   202	  rejected as model-unavailable → the next entry on the same platform is
   203	  selected, with no platform-wide avoidance.
   204	  All platforms/entries exhausted → the loop parks with a resume-at hint
   205	  instead of dying.
   206	- **Caps**: every gate loops at most 5 iterations; on exhaustion the loop
   207	  parks and escalates (writes `.handoff/loop/ESCALATION.md`, notifies) — never
   208	  a 6th run.
   209	
   210	### `baton pipeline` (Layer 3 — a loop preset)
   211	
   212	- `baton pipeline run` = `loop run` with the dual-worktree subtask cycle:
   213	  - Two persistent worktrees `.worktrees/wt-a`, `.worktrees/wt-b`
   214	    (`git worktree add`); `pipeline init` ensure-lines `.worktrees/` into
   215	    `.gitignore` (same idempotent machinery as the `.handoff/` line).
   216	  - Subtask N: the writer seat implements on a namespaced branch
   217	    (`baton/wt-<seat>/subtask-N`) in its worktree; the reviewer seat reviews
   218	    the diff from the OTHER worktree (fresh checkout, fresh context). Seats
   219	    swap every subtask: worker-a writes / worker-b reviews → worker-b writes /
   220	    worker-a reviews → … (concrete models per seat come from the role
   221	    matrix — see Role-matrix additions).
   222	  - Verdict flow: APPROVED → the merger role adversarially re-checks and
   223	    merges into main (the ONLY writer to main); BLOCKED → writer fixes,
   224	    ≤5 iterations, then escalate. After each merge both worktrees
   225	    fast-forward.
   226	
   227	  **Worktree transaction layer (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 5)** —
   228	  `worktrees.mjs` treats every git operation as a guarded transaction:
   229	  - Branch namespace `baton/wt-*/…` is loop-owned; anything else is never
   230	    touched.

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	/**
     2	 * Pure, explainable role resolution over the committed matrix. Every decision
     3	 * is auditable: chosen entries carry their chainIndex; passed-over entries land
     4	 * in skipped[] with a why. avoid[] population is the caller's job.
     5	 * @param {{config: any, to: string, avoid?: string[], avoidEntries?: Array<{platform: string, model: string}>, nativeOnly?: boolean, probes?: Record<string, {capability: string, outcome: string}> | null}} input
     6	 * @returns {{assignments: Record<string, any>, notes: string[]}}
     7	 */
     8	export function resolveRoles({ config, to, avoid = [], avoidEntries = [], nativeOnly = false, probes = null }) {
     9	  /** @type {string[]} */
    10	  const notes = [];
    11	
    12	  /**
    13	   * The eligibility verdict for a platform, or null when eligible.
    14	   * @param {string} platform @returns {string | null}
    15	   */
    16	  function skipReason(platform) {
    17	    if (avoid.includes(platform)) return 'avoided';
    18	    if (!(platform in (config.platforms ?? {}))) return 'unknown-platform';
    19	    if (config.platforms[platform]?.enabled === false) return 'disabled';
    20	    if (probes && probes[platform]) {
    21	      const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    22	      if (outcome === 'rate-limited') return 'rate-limited';
    23	      if (capability === 'not-installed') return 'not-installed';
    24	      // 'installed' means installation was PROVEN but the probe was capped there
    25	      // (capOnSuccess) — authentication is UNVERIFIED, not verified-failed. Only
    26	      // a probe that ran and did NOT succeed (outcome !== 'ok') is a verified
    27	      // auth/reachability failure worth skipping; a capped success stays
    28	      // selectable and is flagged degraded below (iter-3 F1, plan §Role matrix).
    29	      if (capability === 'installed' && outcome !== 'ok') return 'unauthenticated';
    30	    }
    31	    return null;
    32	  }
    33	
    34	  // A selection is degraded when its availability is UNVERIFIED (gate-2 iter-2
    35	  // M3, iter-3 F1): with no probe cache at all, resolution is offline and EVERY
    36	  // selection is degraded (plan: "Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged
    37	  // degraded"); with a partial cache, platforms the cache is missing are; and a
    38	  // platform probed only to 'installed' (auth unverified, e.g. a --version
    39	  // success) is degraded even though it stays selectable.
    40	  /** @param {string} platform */
    41	  const probeUnverified = (platform) => {
    42	    if (probes == null || !probes[platform]) return true;
    43	    const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    44	    // Degraded when ANY required dimension is unverified: a capped 'installed'
    45	    // (auth never confirmed) OR a non-ok outcome (iter-4 I6) — a selectable
    46	    // platform whose last probe ERRORED or TIMED OUT is presented as
    47	    // reachability-verified otherwise, which is exactly the silent-degradation
    48	    // the plan's degraded flag exists to surface. (rate-limited is skipped, not
    49	    // selected, so it never reaches here.)
    50	    return capability === 'installed' || outcome !== 'ok';
    51	  };
    52	
    53	  // Entry-level avoidance (plan §Model-level failover): a specific
    54	  // {platform, model} tuple is dead (e.g. account-tier rejected) while its
    55	  // platform stays usable. Matching is on model IDENTITY — an @effort suffix
    56	  // on either side is ignored — and requires BOTH dimensions, so the same
    57	  // model name on another platform is never caught.
    58	  /** @param {any} m */
    59	  const baseModel = (m) => (typeof m === 'string' ? m.split('@')[0] : m);
    60	  /** @param {string} platform @param {string} model */
    61	  const entryAvoided = (platform, model) =>
    62	    avoidEntries.some((a) => a?.platform === platform && baseModel(a?.model) === baseModel(model));
    63	
    64	  /** @type {Record<string, any>} */
    65	  const assignments = {};
    66	  for (const [role, chain] of Object.entries(config.roles)) {
    67	    /** @type {any[]} */
    68	    const skipped = [];
    69	    /** @type {any} */
    70	    let assignment = null;
    71	
    72	    for (let i = 0; i < chain.length; i += 1) {
    73	      const entry = chain[i];
    74	      if (nativeOnly && entry.platform !== to) {
    75	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'non-native' });
    76	        continue;
    77	      }
    78	      const why = skipReason(entry.platform);
    79	      if (why) {
    80	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why });
    81	        continue;
    82	      }
    83	      // After skipReason so a dual match keeps the platform-level label.
    84	      if (entryAvoided(entry.platform, entry.model)) {
    85	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'avoided-entry' });
    86	        continue;
    87	      }
    88	      assignment = {
    89	        platform: entry.platform,
    90	        model: entry.model,
    91	        effort: entry.effort ?? null,
    92	        mode: entry.platform === to ? 'native' : 'delegated',
    93	        chainIndex: i,
    94	        skipped,
    95	      };
    96	      if (probeUnverified(entry.platform)) assignment.degraded = true;
    97	      break;
    98	    }
    99	
   100	    if (!assignment && nativeOnly) {
   101	      // Forced-default is only valid when the destination itself is eligible.
   102	      const whyTo = skipReason(to);
   103	      const model = config.defaults?.[to];
   104	      if (!whyTo && typeof model === 'string') {
   105	        assignment = { platform: to, model, effort: null, mode: 'forced-default', chainIndex: null, skipped };
   106	        if (probeUnverified(to)) assignment.degraded = true;
   107	      }
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    if (!assignment) {
   111	      assignment = { platform: null, model: null, effort: null, mode: 'unavailable', chainIndex: null, skipped };
   112	    }
   113	    assignments[role] = assignment;
   114	  }
   115	
   116	  return { assignments, notes };
   117	}

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	/**
     2	 * Load + validate baton.config.json, parsing role chains from their
     3	 * "platform/model[@effort]" string form into structured entries.
     4	 * Never throws: returns {config, errors} with dotted-path errors.
     5	 * @param {string} cwd @param {any} io
     6	 * @returns {{config: any | null, errors: {path: string, msg: string}[]}}
     7	 */
     8	export function loadConfig(cwd, io) {
     9	  const file = `${cwd}/baton.config.json`;
    10	  /** @type {{path: string, msg: string}[]} */
    11	  const errors = [];
    12	
    13	  let raw;
    14	  try {
    15	    raw = io.fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
    16	  } catch {
    17	    return { config: null, errors: [{ path: '', msg: `baton.config.json not found at ${file} — run 'baton init' to scaffold it` }] };
    18	  }
    19	  let parsed;
    20	  try {
    21	    parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
    22	  } catch (err) {
    23	    return { config: null, errors: [{ path: '', msg: `baton.config.json is not valid JSON (${/** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? 'parse error'})` }] };
    24	  }
    25	
    26	  if (parsed.roles === null || typeof parsed.roles !== 'object' || Array.isArray(parsed.roles)) {
    27	    errors.push({ path: 'roles', msg: 'roles must be an object mapping role names to chain arrays' });
    28	  }
    29	
    30	  /** @type {Record<string, any[]>} */
    31	  const roles = {};
    32	  if (errors.length === 0) {
    33	    for (const [role, chain] of Object.entries(parsed.roles)) {
    34	      if (!Array.isArray(chain)) {
    35	        errors.push({ path: `roles.${role}`, msg: 'a role chain must be an array of "platform/model[@effort]" strings' });
    36	        continue;
    37	      }
    38	      /** @type {any[]} */
    39	      const entries = [];
    40	      for (let i = 0; i < chain.length; i += 1) {
    41	        const s = chain[i];
    42	        const slash = typeof s === 'string' ? s.indexOf('/') : -1;
    43	        if (slash <= 0 || slash === s.length - 1) {
    44	          errors.push({ path: `roles.${role}[${i}]`, msg: `malformed chain entry ${JSON.stringify(s)} — expected "platform/model[@effort]"` });
    45	          continue;
    46	        }
    47	        const platform = s.slice(0, slash);
    48	        const rest = s.slice(slash + 1);
    49	        const at = rest.indexOf('@');
    50	        const model = at === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, at);
    51	        const effort = at === -1 ? null : rest.slice(at + 1);
    52	        if (parsed.platforms && !(platform in parsed.platforms)) {
    53	          errors.push({ path: `roles.${role}[${i}]`, msg: `unknown platform "${platform}" — not a key of config.platforms` });
    54	          continue;
    55	        }
    56	        entries.push({ platform, model, effort });
    57	      }
    58	      roles[role] = entries;
    59	    }
    60	  }
    61	
    62	  if (errors.length > 0) return { config: null, errors };
    63	  return { config: { ...parsed, roles }, errors };
    64	}

     3	/**
     4	 * The --json contract: exactly one compact envelope line on stdout, nothing else.
     5	 * @param {any} io
     6	 * @param {{ok: boolean, data?: any, warnings?: any[], error?: {code: string, msg: string} | null}} env
     7	 */
     8	export function emitEnvelope(io, env) {
     9	  const full = { ok: env.ok, data: env.data ?? null, warnings: env.warnings ?? [], error: env.error ?? null };
    10	  io.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(full) + '\n');
    11	}
    12	
    13	/**
    14	 * Centralized usage-error emission (gate-2 fix 11): with --json the envelope
    15	 * contract holds even for bad invocations; otherwise a one-line stderr
    16	 * message. Always returns the usage exit code 2.
    17	 * @param {any} io @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags
    18	 * @param {string} cmd @param {string} msg
    19	 * @returns {number}
    20	 */
    21	export function usageError(io, flags, cmd, msg) {
    22	  if (flags.json === true) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'usage', msg } });
    23	  else io.stderr.write(`baton ${cmd}: ${msg}\n`);
    24	  return 2;
    25	}

    27	/**
    28	 * Repo-root discovery (plan §Root discovery): `--root` wins; else the nearest
    29	 * ancestor of io.cwd carrying `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`; else the
    30	 * nearest ancestor carrying `.git` (the repo toplevel — and a boundary the
    31	 * walk never crosses, so a nested repo resolves to itself); else io.cwd.
    32	 * @param {any} io @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags
    33	 * @returns {string}
    34	 */
    35	export function resolveRoot(io, flags) {
    36	  if (typeof flags.root === 'string' && flags.root.length > 0) return flags.root;
    37	  // Normalize separators up front (gate-2 iter-2 M2): a Windows cwd arrives
    38	  // backslash-separated, but Node fs accepts forward slashes, so the ascent
    39	  // and the marker checks work in one forward-slash space. The last separator
    40	  // is either kind; the loop stops at a drive/UNC or filesystem root.
    41	  const start = normSep(io.cwd);
    42	  let dir = start;
    43	  while (true) {
    44	    try {
    45	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.handoff')) || io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, 'baton.config.json'))) return dir;
    46	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.git'))) return dir; // repo toplevel; never walk past a .git boundary
    47	    } catch {
    48	      break;
    49	    }
    50	    const cut = dir.lastIndexOf('/');
    51	    if (cut < 0) break;
    52	    const parent = cut === 0 ? '/' : dir.slice(0, cut);
    53	    // At a drive-relative ceiling ("C:") examine the drive ROOT ("C:/") once —
    54	    // a repo can live directly at C:/ (iter-3 F6) — then stop.
    55	    if (/^[A-Za-z]:$/.test(parent)) {
    56	      const driveRoot = `${parent}/`;
    57	      if (driveRoot !== dir) {
    58	        dir = driveRoot;
    59	        continue;
    60	      }
    61	      break;
    62	    }
    63	    if (parent === dir) break;
    64	    dir = parent;
    65	  }
    66	  return start;
    67	}

    84	export const PLATFORMS = ['claude-code', 'codex', 'cursor'];
    85	
    86	/**
    87	 * Validate a platform id against the enum (surface-audit fold): a typo'd
    88	 * platform used to silently seed persistent state whose bogus origin then
    89	 * rejected the REAL platform's checkpoints as foreign.
    90	 * @param {string | boolean | undefined} value
    91	 * @returns {string | null} an error message, or null when valid/absent
    92	 */
    93	export function platformError(value) {
    94	  if (value === undefined) return null;
    95	  if (typeof value === 'string' && PLATFORMS.includes(value)) return null;
    96	  return `platform must be one of ${PLATFORMS.join('|')} (got ${JSON.stringify(value)})`;
    97	}

    99	/**
   100	 * Strict flag parser (surface-audit fold; docs/design/core.md §tooling always
   101	 * specified strict parsing). spec maps each flag name to 'string' | 'boolean';
   102	 * `json` and `root` are implied common flags. Errors — unknown flag, stray
   103	 * positional, missing string-flag value — return {error} so the command exits
   104	 * 2 instead of silently losing intent: the lenient parser let a stray token
   105	 * flip SAFETY flags off (checkpoint/doctor --strict, remap --native-only,
   106	 * receive --print-prompt all read fail-dangerous exit 0).
   107	 * @param {string[]} args
   108	 * @param {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} spec
   109	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, error?: string}}
   110	 */
   111	export function parseFlagsStrict(args, spec) {
   112	  /** @type {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} */
   113	  const full = { json: 'boolean', root: 'string', ...spec };
   114	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
   115	  const flags = {};
   116	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
   117	    const a = args[i];
   118	    if (!a.startsWith('--')) return { flags, error: `unexpected argument '${a}' — flags are --name [value]` };
   119	    const key = a.slice(2);
   120	    const kind = full[key];
   121	    if (kind === undefined) return { flags, error: `unknown flag --${key}` };
   122	    if (kind === 'boolean') {
   123	      // A following token that is not a flag would have been this flag's
   124	      // silent "value" under the lenient parser; reject it loudly.
   125	      const next = args[i + 1];
   126	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
   127	        return { flags, error: `unexpected token '${next}' after --${key} (a bare flag takes no value)` };
   128	      }
   129	      flags[key] = true;
   130	      continue;
   131	    }
   132	    const next = args[i + 1];
   133	    // A string flag consumes the next token unless it is itself a KNOWN flag
   134	    // (so `--commit --origin x` errors instead of eating '--origin').
   135	    if (next === undefined || (next.startsWith('--') && full[next.slice(2)] !== undefined)) {
   136	      return { flags, error: `--${key} requires a value` };
   137	    }
   138	    flags[key] = next;
   139	    i += 1;
   140	  }
   141	  return { flags };
   142	}
   143	
   144	/**
   145	 * Minimal flag parser: `--key value` pairs (value = next token not starting
   146	 * with --), bare `--key` booleans, positionals collected in order.
   147	 * @param {string[]} args
   148	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, positionals: string[]}}
   149	 */
   150	export function parseFlags(args) {
   151	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
   152	  const flags = {};
   153	  /** @type {string[]} */
   154	  const positionals = [];
   155	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
   156	    const a = args[i];
   157	    if (a.startsWith('--')) {
   158	      const key = a.slice(2);
   159	      const next = args[i + 1];
   160	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
   161	        flags[key] = next;
   162	        i += 1;
   163	      } else {
   164	        flags[key] = true;
   165	      }
   166	    } else {
   167	      positionals.push(a);
   168	    }
   169	  }
   170	  return { flags, positionals };
   171	}

    15	/** @param {any} matcher @param {string} text */
    16	function matches(matcher, text) {
    17	  switch (matcher.kind) {
    18	    case 'substring':
    19	      return text.includes(matcher.value);
    20	    case 'regex':
    21	      return new RegExp(matcher.pattern, matcher.flags || '').test(text);
    22	    case 'json-field': {
    23	      for (const line of text.split('\n')) {
    24	        let obj;
    25	        try {
    26	          obj = JSON.parse(line);
    27	        } catch {
    28	          continue;
    29	        }
    30	        const val = String(matcher.path)
    31	          .split('.')
    32	          .reduce((o, k) => (o == null ? undefined : o[k]), obj);
    33	        if (val === matcher.equals) return true;
    34	      }
    35	      return false;
    36	    }
    37	    default:
    38	      return false;
    39	  }
    40	}
    41	
    42	/**
    43	 * Classify harness output. Structured evidence first (text and exit code are
    44	 * ignored when a recognized structured signal is present); text signatures as
    45	 * the fallback tier; exit code only breaks the no-match tie — a generic nonzero
    46	 * exit is never usage-limit on its own.
    47	 * @param {{text?: string, exitCode?: number, platform: string, table: any, structured?: {kind: string, errorType: string} | null}} input
    48	 * @returns {{class: string, signatureId: string | null, confidence: string | null, resetHint: string | null, tried?: string[]}}
    49	 */
    50	export function classify({ text = '', exitCode = 0, platform, table, structured = null }) {
    51	  if (structured) {
    52	    if (structured.kind === 'stop-failure') {
    53	      const cls = STOP_FAILURE_MAP[structured.errorType] ?? 'other-error';
    54	      return { class: cls, signatureId: `structured:${structured.errorType}`, confidence: 'high', resetHint: null };
    55	    }
    56	    if (structured.kind === 'exec-json') {
    57	      const cls = structured.errorType === 'usage_limit' ? 'usage-limit' : 'other-error';
    58	      return { class: cls, signatureId: `structured:${structured.errorType}`, confidence: 'high', resetHint: null };
    59	    }
    60	    // Unrecognized structured kind: fall through to the text tier.
    61	  }
    62	
    63	  const stripped = text.replace(ANSI, '');
    64	  const candidates = table.signatures.filter((/** @type {any} */ s) => s.platform === platform);
    65	  /** @type {any} */
    66	  let best = null;
    67	  for (const s of candidates) {
    68	    if (!matches(s.matcher, stripped)) continue;
    69	    if (best === null || PRECEDENCE.indexOf(s.class) < PRECEDENCE.indexOf(best.class)) best = s;
    70	  }
    71	
    72	  if (best) {
    73	    let resetHint = null;
    74	    if (typeof best.resetHint === 'string') {
    75	      const m = stripped.match(new RegExp(best.resetHint));
    76	      if (m) resetHint = m[1] ?? m[0];
    77	    }
    78	    return { class: best.class, signatureId: best.id, confidence: best.confidence, resetHint };
    79	  }
    80	
    81	  return {
    82	    class: exitCode !== 0 ? 'other-error' : 'ok',
    83	    signatureId: null,
    84	    confidence: null,
    85	    resetHint: null,
    86	  };
    87	}
